metadata.subject: Tiếng Anh
metadata.textbook: Kết nối tri thức với cuộc sống
metadata.localGuidelines: Đề kiểm tra Tiếng Anh 12 gồm đầy đủ kỹ năng Listening (kèm Tapescript cho giáo viên), Lexico-Grammar, Reading Comprehension và Sentence Transformation/Writing. Phân bổ: 16 câu MCQ (4,0đ), 2 bài Đúng/Sai Listening & Reading (2 câu × 4 ý = 2,0đ), 4 câu Trả lời ngắn/Điền từ (2,0đ), 2 câu Viết lại câu/Đoạn văn ngắn (2,0đ). Tổng = 10,0 điểm.

questions.explanation: Dr. Jenkins states: "many megacities have started replacing single-use plastics with biodegradable materials".

Replacing all traditional customs with foreign habits

questions.stem: [LISTENING TRUE/FALSE] Listen to the interview with Dr. Sarah Jenkins and decide whether the following statements are True (Đ) or False (S):

statements.text: Dr. Sarah Jenkins is an urban environmentalist.
Dr. Jenkins believes that adopting a green lifestyle is always too expensive for students.
Unplugging electronic devices when not in use is one of the habits recommended in the podcast.
More than 4,500 high school students participated in the "Zero-Waste Campus" campaign in Singapore.

questions.explanation: a) True; b) False (she says simple daily habits are inexpensive and effective); c) True; d) True (Over 4,500 high school students joined).

items.text: Dr. Sarah Jenkins is an urban environmentalist.
Dr. Jenkins believes that adopting a green lifestyle is always too expensive for students.
Unplugging electronic devices when not in use is one of the habits recommended in the podcast.
More than 4,500 high school students participated in the "Zero-Waste Campus" campaign in Singapore.

Rewrite the following sentence using the Double Comparative structure ("The more..., the more..."):
"If a city plants more trees, its air becomes cleaner."
questions.answer: The more trees a city plants, the cleaner its air becomes.
questions.explanation: Scoring rubric (1.0 point): Correct double comparative structure "The more trees a city plants, the cleaner its air becomes" (1.0 pt).

questions.stem: Write a short paragraph (100 – 120 words) about three practical ways high school students can practice Green Living at school and at home.
questions.answer: Paragraph (100-120 words) discussing 3 green habits: reducing single-use plastic, saving energy, and sorting waste.
questions.explanation:
Scoring rubric (1.0 point):
- Task achievement & 3 clear practical ways (0.4 pt)
- Coherence, cohesion & connectors (First, Second, Finally...) (0.3 pt)
- Vocabulary & grammar accuracy on Green Living (0.3 pt).

readingPassage:
Read the following passage about Cultural Diversity and Urbanisation and answer the questions:
In the 21st century, rapid urbanisation has brought people from diverse cultural backgrounds together into vibrant metropolitan areas. While moving to big cities offers young workers better job opportunities, modern healthcare, and higher education, it also creates pressure on housing and public infrastructure. At the same time, preserving traditional festivals, local cuisine, and community values helps citizens maintain their cultural identity in a globalised world.
listeningTranscript:
[TAPESCRIPT FOR LISTENING SECTION - TEACHER'S COPY]
Host: Welcome to "Green Future Podcast". Today we are talking with Dr. Sarah Jenkins, an urban environmentalist, about Green Living and Sustainable Cities.
Dr. Sarah Jenkins: Thank you! Over the past decade, many megacities have started replacing single-use plastics with biodegradable materials and expanding electric public transport networks.
Host: What is the biggest challenge for young people who want to adopt a green lifestyle?
Dr. Sarah Jenkins: Many students think green living is expensive. However, simple daily habits like bringing a reusable water bottle, unplugging electronic devices when not in use, and sorting household waste can reduce a household's carbon footprint by up to 25 percent every year.
Host: Did your recent project in Singapore show positive results?
Dr. Sarah Jenkins: Yes! Over 4,500 high school students joined our "Zero-Waste Campus" campaign in 2025, collecting 12 tons of recyclable paper and plastic within just three months.
